defects.summary: Delegation power is never checked: grant_delegation lets any principal delegate permissions it does not hold, so a low-privilege subject can grant itself privilege through a group (confused deputy / privilege escalation).
defects.trigger: grant_delegation(delegator, group_id, perms) inserts without verifying delegator holds perms.
defects.consequence: Any authenticated subject can obtain permissions it was never granted.
defects.evidence: acl.py: grant_delegation body; design.md 'Delegation power' section.
defects.smallest_correction: Reject grant_delegation unless effective_permissions(delegator) contains every perm in perms (checked at grant time).

defects.summary: Revocation is not immediate: effective_permissions serves cached pre-revocation results until the 300-second sweep, violating the 'revocation must be immediate, never stale' constraint.
defects.trigger: revoke_delegation only clears the cache; cached entries are still served while their expiry is in the future.
defects.consequence: A revoked delegation remains effective for up to 300 seconds.
defects.evidence: acl.py: effective_permissions cache hit path; design.md 'Cache' section.
defects.smallest_correction: Invalidate the affected subject entries synchronously on revocation (or remove the cache and compute per authorization).

false_positive_pool.summary: Suggest adding a permissive admin override flag to bypass delegation checks for support staff.
